issues: Accessibility – role-img-alt missing on tab bar icons. In expo-app/App.tsx the FontAwesome icons used for the bottom Tab.Navigator do not provide proper alternative text on the web (they render as <div role="img"> without alt/aria-label). Add accessible={true}, accessibilityLabel and accessibilityRole="image" (or use an <Image> with alt) to each FontAwesome component used in tabBarIcon to satisfy the accessibility check.

Email enumeration – backend/app/main.py signup endpoint returns a distinct 400 error when an email is already registered, enabling attackers to enumerate accounts. Change the logic to always return a generic success response (e.g., 200 with a generic message) and perform email verification asynchronously, without revealing existence of the email.

OpenAPI schema exposure – backend/app/main.py creates FastAPI with openapi_url="/openapi.json" which is publicly accessible. To avoid leaking endpoint signatures, set openapi_url=None (or protect the endpoint with authentication or IP‑based restrictions). This also aligns with the security checklist.

Unauthenticated media endpoint rate limiting – backend/app/main.py /media/{filename} endpoint is only protected by authentication but lacks any rate‑limiting, allowing token‑holders to flood the endpoint. Add a @limiter.limit decorator (e.g., "10/minute") to the get_media route.

Decompression‑bomb image attack – _validate_image in backend/app/main.py validates image type and size but does not limit image dimensions or pixel count. Before calling Image.open, set Pillow's Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS to a safe limit (e.g., 10_000_000) and reject images exceeding it, or explicitly check width/height and reject overly large images.

Insecure token storage on web – expo-app/src/auth.ts (not shown) stores the JWT in AsyncStorage/localStorage, which is accessible to JavaScript and vulnerable to XSS. Update the auth helper to store the token in an httpOnly, Secure cookie on web (or use a web‑compatible secure storage library) and keep secure storage on native via expo-secure-store.

Medium dependency vulnerabilities – expo-app/package.json still includes dependencies with known CVEs: sprintf-js (CVE‑2026‑97058) and uuid (CVE‑2026‑41907). Upgrade sprintf-js to a non‑vulnerable version (or replace with native template literals) and upgrade uuid to >=13.0.1 (or latest 13.x) to resolve the issues. Ensure the lockfile reflects the safe versions.
feedback: The core functionality (FastAPI backend, JWT auth, receipt/mileage CRUD, dashboard, export, Expo UI flow) works and all acceptance tests pass. However, there are several serious problems that block the submission: missing alternative text for images (accessibility), email enumeration, public OpenAPI schema, missing rate limiting on media, potential image decompression‑bomb vulnerability, insecure JWT storage on the web, and remaining medium‑severity dependency vulnerabilities. Address the listed issues by updating the relevant files and configurations, then re‑run the tests and static validation.
